paraphrase: Argues that perfect verification backfires: when everything is verified, verification signals nothing. Introduces concepts of verification fatigue (too much signal, nobody looks), verification as signal (signals replace actual verification), and trust ceiling (verification cannot exceed the trustworthiness of what it reports on).

claims.text: Perfect verification makes verification meaningless — when 100% of decisions are verified, verification signals nothing
claims.notes: Core paradox: verification derives value from scarcity

claims.text: Every verification system bottoms out at a trust ceiling — it must trust itself at some point to get started
evidence_refs: comment by xkai reinforcing this point

evaluation.notes: Changes framing: the problem isn't just what fields, but whether anyone actually reads them. Links to agentstamp comment about uniform receipt schema collapsing signal.
